thread.title: BlackBerry: The Roller Coaster Ride Is Not Yet Over - BlackBerry Ltd. (NYSE:BB)

author: KIA Investment Research
title: BlackBerry: The Roller Coaster Ride Is Not Yet Over - BlackBerry Ltd. (NYSE:BB)
text:
Long-suffering BlackBerry ( BB ) has more pain in store, and quite frankly, I don't see any way to avoid it.
The problem is the auto industry's move away from BlackBerry's relatively primitive QNX operating system, the operating system that powers most cars' infotainment systems.
Infotainment systems are those computers most of us have in our cars that run things like maps, CD/radio, air conditioning, etc. But there is a movement afoot to drastically improve infotainment systems and imbue them with the same bells and whistles you find on smartphones today.
I began cautioning BlackBerry investors 3 years ago about the impending arrival of rich infotainment that would look more like a smartphone and include an app store. And just last year , I even went so far as to suggest BlackBerry roll their own Android-based infotainment system since they already have an Android build of their own. But this was not to be.
Others though have taken the Android threat/opportunity seriously. Today, we can see the actual implementation of these state-of-the-art systems in Android P-powered infotainment. And, they are amazing.
Source : engadget.com
Part of this month's Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) I/O developer conference was a demo of native Android P powering Volvo's XC40 infotainment system. And we're not talking about Android Auto either. This isn't Android running on a smartphone, then being cast upon the infotainment screen. This is 100% Google Android P running atop Volvo hardware with a Volvo skin (minute mark 1:50).
Android execs have said they are deprecating the use of their own in-house OS (QNX) in favor of Android. They went on to say that, at least for now, "this is the best experience you are going to get in a vehicle." (minute mark 0:50).
And I can believe that. This infotainment system is beautiful, and if you are an Android user, you will feel right at home with the user experience. Oh, and if you're worried about Apple CarPlay (NASDAQ: AAPL ), fear not. Despite Android and iOS being mortal enemies, embedded Android will continue to let iPhone users mirror their screens on the dash.
Google's Maps completely replaces Volvo's own navigation system. You can also jump into your media or other apps while Maps navigation is running since the turn-by-turn readout is also pushed to a secondary display in the middle of the dashboard.
But aren't apps dangerous in a car? One of the sour-grapes arguments BlackBerry bulls like to use against having an apps store available in-vehicle (since QNX doesn't have one) is that having apps in a car is dangerous!
Here is what Google has to say on the matter:
Poke around the tablet long enough and you'll find a Play Store icon that ushers you into Google's in-car marketplace . It's definitely not the Play Store you're probably used to, though: Google told us there are "thousands of apps" that have been pre-approved for use on in-car Android systems , though most of the ones I got to try were streaming services like Spotify and Deezer. There are a few limitations to keep in mind, though. For one, Google says - for now, anyway - that you can't download and install apps while you're driving. Fair enough. It's important to note that you more than likely can't interact with some apps the way you would on your smartphone, either. We're told that you couldn't, say, skim through the entirety of your Google Play Music library on the touchscreen to find a song - the experience is limited to a couple of different interactions that are already enabled in Android Auto today. For that, you're better off holding down a button on the steering wheel and asking Google Assistant for some help. (emphasis added.)
Source : engadget.com
To my thinking, though, it's better to have a large screen in your line-of-site, designed with single-touch interactions in mind, than a little screen designed for two-handed use and multi-touch.
In the end, though, it really doesn't matter what rationalization one chooses. App stores for the car are here and QNX 1) doesn't have one to speak of, and 2) QNX cannot attract the developers to support the platform (as evidenced by the catastrophic failure of BlackBerry's BB10 operating system.)
Why BlackBerry can no longer compete in this space Primarily, due to advances in user experience, (Google and Apple dominate here,) and application developer support (again, Google and Apple.)
Google has far more experience in creating a beautiful user experience, first-class security, and has arguably the largest developer community on the planet .
How important is infotainment to BlackBerry?
According to BlackBerry's 2018 Q4 results , BlackBerry is #1 in infotainment and in some 60 million vehicles. This seems impressive. But if we look at the rate of growth, it's far less impressive.
BlackBerry achieved installations in some 50 million vehicles way back in 2015. With 60 million announced in 2018, we can see that growth in the segment has all but stalled. Indeed, that's only a 6.5% increase per year. Add to that the fact that several car manufacturers 1 , 2 , 3 have announced new Android-based infotainment. We could likely be looking at a trend reversal in the making.
QNX makes up the largest portion of BlackBerry's BlackBerry Technology Solutions or BTS, and BTS makes up 19.2% of revenue.
Source : 40-F annual report :
A serious decay in QNX infotainment licenses will have a serious impact on BlackBerry's bottom line.
Being someone that understands and appreciates state-of-the-art technology, I can't see people preferring a primitive, app-less/app-store-less, infotainment system when they can have essentially a smartphone experience in their car without a need to connect a smartphone!
Wrapping up With BlackBerry's turnaround now complete , no hope of challenging Android infotainment, and a chart that looks like this, I find almost nothing to get excited about.
Source : finviz.com
We're back to where we were in 2013, 2014, and 2015!
Investor Takeaway If your BlackBerry investment thesis is based at least in part on BlackBerry's ability to dominate, or even maintain, its dominance in infotainment , please carefully consider the information provided in this note.
